top_news.title: Belgium: Clashes break out between protesters, police amid agitation against rising cost of living in parts of Europe
top_news.summary: Clashes broke out between protesters and the police in Brussels and Lige in Belgium on Saturday as agitation against the rising cost of living rattled parts of Europe, Euronews reported. According to Euronews, police used water cannons against protesters, who were seen throwing objects, including water bottles, at the security forces. Belgian Interior Minister Bernard Quintin described it as pure and simple violence, organised and repeated to destabilise our society and termed the protesters as rioters. NO, what is unfolding in Brussels is no longer mere protest! It is pure and simple violence, organised and repeated to destabilise our society. The federal police are in support of the local police. All necessary means will be used to restore order in the face of the rioters, Quintin posted on X. Agitation in France, which began with protests against the condition of school infrastructure and alleged budget cuts in the education sector, turned into a massive protest over rising fuel prices and cost of living. French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told France 24 that 5,50,000 people took part in the protests against dwindling purchasing power, with 1,10,000 demonstrators in the capital. Police have arrested 400 protesters over vandalism charges, he said. French President Emmanuel Macron has expressed a firm response to violence amid the ongoing protests, driven primarily by students who, over the past few weeks, have engaged in violent demonstrations to denounce what they call deplorable school conditions and excessive police force. In a post on X, Macron vowed strict action against the protestors who were involved in vandalism and looting, expressing solidarity against sowers of chaos. No room for violence in our Republic. Those who have broken, attacked the prefectures as well as businesses, looted even our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished. To the law enforcement forces, guarantors of the right to demonstrate, I express the support of the Nation. We will all stand united against the sowers of chaos, who seek only to bring down our institutions and prevent those who peacefully express their demands from doing so, he wrote. French media has reported that former 'Yellow Vest' figures are set to join the protests in support of high-school students. 'Yellow Vest' movement began in 2018 in France, bringing thousands of people to the streets against rising fuel prices and economic inequality. The protests were met with rubber bullets fired by the police, injuring more than 2,500 protesters and 1,800 police personnel in the clashes. Meanwhile in Italy, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni issued a firm condemnation of violent demonstrations across major cities, declaring that while peaceful protest is fundamental to democratic society, political violence and destruction will not be tolerated. In a statement posted on X addressing recent nationwide rallies, Meloni drew a sharp contrast between peaceful demonstrators and violent agitators who turned city streets into scenes of unrest. I have great respect for the thousands of people who today demonstrated peacefully, including those who took part in the mobilisation called by the CGIL, which also saw the participation of left-wing leaders, Meloni said. Whatever the ideas for which one demonstrates, participation is the foundation of any healthy democracy. The demonstrations organised by the Italy in the Square committee devolved into severe clashes, mass detentions, and property destruction, Italian broadcaster Rai News reported. (ANI)

top_news.title: West Bengal stampede a
top_news.summary: Telangana BJP President N Ramchander Rao on Sunday termed the stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata that claimed 19 lives a major tragedy and called for a thorough probe to fix responsibility and take action against those responsible. Condoling the deaths, Rao said the incident required a proper investigation and that accountability must be established. The stampede in West Bengal, in Kolkata, is a big tragedy, and I condole the deaths of the devotees there. I'm sure that the government will definitely probe the entire incident, fix responsibility on the people who are responsible for it, and take appropriate action, Rao told ANI. Referring to the West Bengal government's response, he said the administration was concerned about the incident and stressed the need for accountability. As declared by Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari ji, everyone is concerned about the entire incident. A proper probe should definitely be conducted, and action must be taken against those who are responsible, he added. The stampede occurred at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in North Kolkata amid heavy crowds, killing 19 people and leaving 25 others injured. The injured were shifted to hospitals for treatment, while authorities initiated an investigation into the circumstances leading to the incident. Meanwhile, Kolkata Police arrested seven people in connection with the incident. Those arrested include Raj Kumar Sewda, alias Raja, the secretary of the puja committee; Santanu Dubey, its vice-president; and Biplab Mukherjee, alias Joy, who was involved in the construction of a bamboo structure. The other arrested persons include Koushik Saha, who was involved in crowd management and checking VIP passes; Pintu Dey, who was engaged in crowd management; and Suman Chakraborty and Rajesh Pal, who were working as private security in-charges. Police registered a suo motu case under Sections 105, 110 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) against the organisers and others. Fourteen people were also detained for questioning, according to the police. Meanwhile, Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, was imposed in parts of Kolkata from October 18 to 20 to prevent possible disturbances. The restrictions cover an area under Bowbazar Police Station bounded by College Street, CR Avenue, Collotola Street and Eden Hospital Road. The order prohibits unlawful assemblies of five or more people, carrying weapons and activities likely to disturb public peace and tranquillity. The West Bengal government has announced compensation of Rs 25 lakh and a job for the family of each deceased person. An investigation by the Special Task Force (STF) has also been initiated to establish accountability. In a separate political attack, Rao criticised the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and Opposition leaders over their remarks about regime change. The CJP and other leaders who are now claiming that they are going to fight for regime change, like in Bangladesh, should remember that India is not Bangladesh. India has a very strong and deep-rooted democratic ethos, and I'm sure that the people of this country are observing how these people behave, he said. Rao also accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of making irresponsible statements and attempting to create unrest in the country. Rahul Gandhi is acting very irresponsibly, misleading the people, and trying to create anarchy in the country through his statements and actions, he said. His remarks come amid a political row over references to regime change by opposition leaders and student activists during protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Senior advocate Prashant Bhushan, All India Students Association (AISA) president Neha Bora and Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera have publicly used or discussed the phrase regime change during conferences and press addresses in Delhi in the context of the protests. Student activists, including Bora at a Socialist Students Front conference, also referred to the Gen-Z-led uprising in Bangladesh that led to the ouster of then-Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. The national capital has witnessed a series of Tricolour marches in recent days, with Opposition groups and civil society organisations holding demonstrations against the alleged electoral irregularities. The use of the national flag during these protests has triggered a political confrontation, with the BJP accusing opposition parties of using it to advance their political agitation. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh had accused Congress and its allies of attempting to replicate a Bangladesh-style political upheaval in India. Attempts are being made to turn the country's youth into pawns of anarchic politics. Regime change is being pursued on the lines of Bangladesh, Singh said at a press conference in Lucknow. (ANI)

top_news.title: BRS Working President KTR extends condolences to families of students killed in Nadergul accident
top_news.summary: BRS Working President K T Rama Rao (KTR) expressed grief over the deaths of students in an accident at an engineering college in Nadergul, Telangana, and extended his condolences to the bereaved families. BRS Working President KTR expressed deep sorrow over the death of two students in an accident at MVSR Engineering College in Nadergul. KTR conveyed his heartfelt condolences to the families of the students who lost their lives in this tragic incident, the official statement read. KTR also wished a speedy recovery to the students injured in the incident and urged the authorities to ensure that they receive the best possible medical treatment. Expressing his condolences to the bereaved families, KTR wished them strength and courage to cope with this immense loss and tragedy, it added. The incident occurred on Saturday during a Dandiya celebration at the college as part of its annual technical-cum-cultural festival, 'Sangamam', when a lighting truss collapsed amid strong winds, leaving students injured. Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy also expressed shock over the incident and conveyed his condolences to the family of the deceased student. He directed officials to ensure the best possible medical treatment for the injured and ordered them to identify those responsible for the accident and take strict action against them, according to the Chief Minister's Office (CMO). Meanwhile, BJP leader Andela Sriramulu Yadav alleged negligence on the part of the college management and demanded the arrest of those responsible. Speaking about the incident on Saturday, Yadav said, Today around 6.30 pm, an event was held at MVSR College, and there was negligence. Small poles, about 80 feet high, were erected and they suddenly fell on 20 girls. Four girls are in serious condition. There are reports that two girls have died and two others are in critical condition, while many have sustained injuries. It is very sad. It is truly negligence of MVSR College management. He further alleged that the management had put students' lives at risk and warned that further action would be announced if the police failed to arrest those responsible. The event should have been organised by the college management itself. They have risked students' lives. If the police do not arrest them, we will announce our future course of action tomorrow morning, Yadav said. According to police, the collapse occurred during the Dandiya programme, injuring several students who were subsequently shifted to hospitals for treatment. College Director Prasanna Kumar described the incident as an unforeseen mishap caused by sudden, strong winds. He said the management had arranged vehicles to transport the injured students to the hospital without waiting for ambulances. Police have launched an investigation to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the collapse and determine whether adequate safety measures were in place during the event. (ANI)

articles.title: Belgium: Clashes break out between protesters, police amid agitation against rising cost of living in parts of Europe
articles.summary: Clashes broke out between protesters and the police in Brussels and Lige in Belgium on Saturday as agitation against the rising cost of living rattled parts of Europe, Euronews reported. According to Euronews, police used water cannons against protesters, who were seen throwing objects, including water bottles, at the security forces. Belgian Interior Minister Bernard Quintin described it as pure and simple violence, organised and repeated to destabilise our society and termed the protesters as rioters. NO, what is unfolding in Brussels is no longer mere protest! It is pure and simple violence, organised and repeated to destabilise our society. The federal police are in support of the local police. All necessary means will be used to restore order in the face of the rioters, Quintin posted on X. Agitation in France, which began with protests against the condition of school infrastructure and alleged budget cuts in the education sector, turned into a massive protest over rising fuel prices and cost of living. French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told France 24 that 5,50,000 people took part in the protests against dwindling purchasing power, with 1,10,000 demonstrators in the capital. Police have arrested 400 protesters over vandalism charges, he said. French President Emmanuel Macron has expressed a firm response to violence amid the ongoing protests, driven primarily by students who, over the past few weeks, have engaged in violent demonstrations to denounce what they call deplorable school conditions and excessive police force. In a post on X, Macron vowed strict action against the protestors who were involved in vandalism and looting, expressing solidarity against sowers of chaos. No room for violence in our Republic. Those who have broken, attacked the prefectures as well as businesses, looted even our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished. To the law enforcement forces, guarantors of the right to demonstrate, I express the support of the Nation. We will all stand united against the sowers of chaos, who seek only to bring down our institutions and prevent those who peacefully express their demands from doing so, he wrote. French media has reported that former 'Yellow Vest' figures are set to join the protests in support of high-school students. 'Yellow Vest' movement began in 2018 in France, bringing thousands of people to the streets against rising fuel prices and economic inequality. The protests were met with rubber bullets fired by the police, injuring more than 2,500 protesters and 1,800 police personnel in the clashes. Meanwhile in Italy, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni issued a firm condemnation of violent demonstrations across major cities, declaring that while peaceful protest is fundamental to democratic society, political violence and destruction will not be tolerated. In a statement posted on X addressing recent nationwide rallies, Meloni drew a sharp contrast between peaceful demonstrators and violent agitators who turned city streets into scenes of unrest. I have great respect for the thousands of people who today demonstrated peacefully, including those who took part in the mobilisation called by the CGIL, which also saw the participation of left-wing leaders, Meloni said. Whatever the ideas for which one demonstrates, participation is the foundation of any healthy democracy. The demonstrations organised by the Italy in the Square committee devolved into severe clashes, mass detentions, and property destruction, Italian broadcaster Rai News reported. (ANI)

articles.title: West Bengal stampede a
articles.summary: Telangana BJP President N Ramchander Rao on Sunday termed the stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata that claimed 19 lives a major tragedy and called for a thorough probe to fix responsibility and take action against those responsible. Condoling the deaths, Rao said the incident required a proper investigation and that accountability must be established. The stampede in West Bengal, in Kolkata, is a big tragedy, and I condole the deaths of the devotees there. I'm sure that the government will definitely probe the entire incident, fix responsibility on the people who are responsible for it, and take appropriate action, Rao told ANI. Referring to the West Bengal government's response, he said the administration was concerned about the incident and stressed the need for accountability. As declared by Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari ji, everyone is concerned about the entire incident. A proper probe should definitely be conducted, and action must be taken against those who are responsible, he added. The stampede occurred at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in North Kolkata amid heavy crowds, killing 19 people and leaving 25 others injured. The injured were shifted to hospitals for treatment, while authorities initiated an investigation into the circumstances leading to the incident. Meanwhile, Kolkata Police arrested seven people in connection with the incident. Those arrested include Raj Kumar Sewda, alias Raja, the secretary of the puja committee; Santanu Dubey, its vice-president; and Biplab Mukherjee, alias Joy, who was involved in the construction of a bamboo structure. The other arrested persons include Koushik Saha, who was involved in crowd management and checking VIP passes; Pintu Dey, who was engaged in crowd management; and Suman Chakraborty and Rajesh Pal, who were working as private security in-charges. Police registered a suo motu case under Sections 105, 110 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) against the organisers and others. Fourteen people were also detained for questioning, according to the police. Meanwhile, Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, was imposed in parts of Kolkata from October 18 to 20 to prevent possible disturbances. The restrictions cover an area under Bowbazar Police Station bounded by College Street, CR Avenue, Collotola Street and Eden Hospital Road. The order prohibits unlawful assemblies of five or more people, carrying weapons and activities likely to disturb public peace and tranquillity. The West Bengal government has announced compensation of Rs 25 lakh and a job for the family of each deceased person. An investigation by the Special Task Force (STF) has also been initiated to establish accountability. In a separate political attack, Rao criticised the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and Opposition leaders over their remarks about regime change. The CJP and other leaders who are now claiming that they are going to fight for regime change, like in Bangladesh, should remember that India is not Bangladesh. India has a very strong and deep-rooted democratic ethos, and I'm sure that the people of this country are observing how these people behave, he said. Rao also accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of making irresponsible statements and attempting to create unrest in the country. Rahul Gandhi is acting very irresponsibly, misleading the people, and trying to create anarchy in the country through his statements and actions, he said. His remarks come amid a political row over references to regime change by opposition leaders and student activists during protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Senior advocate Prashant Bhushan, All India Students Association (AISA) president Neha Bora and Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera have publicly used or discussed the phrase regime change during conferences and press addresses in Delhi in the context of the protests. Student activists, including Bora at a Socialist Students Front conference, also referred to the Gen-Z-led uprising in Bangladesh that led to the ouster of then-Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. The national capital has witnessed a series of Tricolour marches in recent days, with Opposition groups and civil society organisations holding demonstrations against the alleged electoral irregularities. The use of the national flag during these protests has triggered a political confrontation, with the BJP accusing opposition parties of using it to advance their political agitation. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh had accused Congress and its allies of attempting to replicate a Bangladesh-style political upheaval in India. Attempts are being made to turn the country's youth into pawns of anarchic politics. Regime change is being pursued on the lines of Bangladesh, Singh said at a press conference in Lucknow. (ANI)

articles.title: BRS Working President KTR extends condolences to families of students killed in Nadergul accident
articles.summary: BRS Working President K T Rama Rao (KTR) expressed grief over the deaths of students in an accident at an engineering college in Nadergul, Telangana, and extended his condolences to the bereaved families. BRS Working President KTR expressed deep sorrow over the death of two students in an accident at MVSR Engineering College in Nadergul. KTR conveyed his heartfelt condolences to the families of the students who lost their lives in this tragic incident, the official statement read. KTR also wished a speedy recovery to the students injured in the incident and urged the authorities to ensure that they receive the best possible medical treatment. Expressing his condolences to the bereaved families, KTR wished them strength and courage to cope with this immense loss and tragedy, it added. The incident occurred on Saturday during a Dandiya celebration at the college as part of its annual technical-cum-cultural festival, 'Sangamam', when a lighting truss collapsed amid strong winds, leaving students injured. Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy also expressed shock over the incident and conveyed his condolences to the family of the deceased student. He directed officials to ensure the best possible medical treatment for the injured and ordered them to identify those responsible for the accident and take strict action against them, according to the Chief Minister's Office (CMO). Meanwhile, BJP leader Andela Sriramulu Yadav alleged negligence on the part of the college management and demanded the arrest of those responsible. Speaking about the incident on Saturday, Yadav said, Today around 6.30 pm, an event was held at MVSR College, and there was negligence. Small poles, about 80 feet high, were erected and they suddenly fell on 20 girls. Four girls are in serious condition. There are reports that two girls have died and two others are in critical condition, while many have sustained injuries. It is very sad. It is truly negligence of MVSR College management. He further alleged that the management had put students' lives at risk and warned that further action would be announced if the police failed to arrest those responsible. The event should have been organised by the college management itself. They have risked students' lives. If the police do not arrest them, we will announce our future course of action tomorrow morning, Yadav said. According to police, the collapse occurred during the Dandiya programme, injuring several students who were subsequently shifted to hospitals for treatment. College Director Prasanna Kumar described the incident as an unforeseen mishap caused by sudden, strong winds. He said the management had arranged vehicles to transport the injured students to the hospital without waiting for ambulances. Police have launched an investigation to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the collapse and determine whether adequate safety measures were in place during the event. (ANI)
